entries.title: More reliable updates
items: Updates now come from Amphora's own download service, so they keep arriving without anyone renewing a separate access token.
Renewing your license is all it takes to keep updates coming: paste the new key under Settings → General.
For IT teams with a firewall allow-list: Amphora now reaches get.amphoracdn.com, registry.amphoracdn.com and pkg-containers.githubusercontent.com.
Settings → General shows a release's date correctly in every time zone.

entries.title: Several options at once, quantities in kits, clear cart, arrives by
items: A product in options: Order several options at once — a quantity for each shade or size, all added to the cart in one go.
Kits: How many under each pick, and per shade — two of one fragrance, three of one shade. Each counts as a pick.
Cart: Clear cart empties it (after a yes), beside removing single lines.
Checkout: Arrives by, from the carrier's own transit times for the address, carrier and service — it moves with rush and the service. Needs a connected UPS or FedEx account.

entries.title: Kits: pick up to the max, several shades of one part
items: A build-your-own kit's max picks is a ceiling: “Pick up to 4” takes one to four, not exactly four.
A buyer's-choice part in shades takes several shades (+ Add another…), each one a pick — two lip oils in different colours. Max picks can count those shades.

entries.title: Kits: printed cards ask for their details, parts in options pick an option
items: A kit with a print-on-demand part (a handwritten card) asks for the card's details on the kit's page, with a live proof; Add to cart waits for them, and they go to the card's print job.
A printed part never makes a kit out of stock or Waiting on parts — it's made for the order.
A kit part that comes in options (shades, sizes) shows in stock when any option has stock, and the buyer picks which option goes in — that option is what's picked and shipped.

entries.title: Fonts in one place, logos from brand guidelines, guides kept for next time, category pictures, two-line examples
items: Settings → Fonts: every font — house and per client — in one list, each drawn in its own face, with what uses it. Rename, move between every client and one client, mark the licence as covering websites, delete what nothing uses.

The same font file uploaded again is the same font — in Settings, the print designer or the portal studio — never a second copy. Copies already there show as one warning with Merge into one; designs and portals using a copy switch to the one kept.
House fonts cleared for websites can be used in any client's portal.

Brand guidelines: the logos in the PDF are found and cut out — a PNG with the background cleared (Use as portal logo) and the guide's page cropped to the logo as a vector PDF for print. Logos on dark panels come out as the light version.
Brand guidelines are kept per client: the studio opens on the last one, the same PDF again isn't read twice, and an AI theme already asked for comes back without asking the AI again.

Category pictures (a category → Make a picture): a name tile set exactly in the portal's font and colours, a picture drawn by AI from the brand, the category and the products in it, or the client's own picture improved. Keep one as the portal's style and later categories follow it — on their own, if you switch that on.
Image generation (Settings → Integrations): OpenAI or Gemini, its own key and model, separate from the AI assistant.
Print designer: a text box that takes more than one line has a multi-line Example — Enter starts a new line, so a closing like “With love,” over the team name looks on the canvas the way it prints.
Portal users → Add a person: Power buyer sits on its own line, so the fields line up.

entries.title: Handwritten notes: your handwriting font, salutation, body and closing, justified
items: Add a font, in the designer under the font list: drop in a licensed TTF or OTF handwriting font. For every client makes it a house font any brand can use.

Handwritten note, on the left of the designer, lays out Salutation, Body, Closing and a small card number in one click, in the library's handwriting font. The type is sized from the font itself, so the note fills the card the same way whichever handwriting font you use.
Justified text: a fourth alignment button. Every line runs edge to edge; a paragraph's last line stays left.
Lists with FirstLine, Body, LastLine and FileName columns (what mail houses send) match the note's fields on their own.

entries.title: 5 × 7 cards, bigger build-a-kits, and a way back from Order placed in Reader view
items: Print setup: Card 5 × 7 is one of the quick sizes, next to Postcard and Large postcard.
Kits take up to 500 parts (it was 50), and Buyer picks up to goes to 500. A kit with 54 buyer's-choice parts was refused with only “Invalid input”.
When a SKU's Save changes is refused, the message names the field and the rule, not just “Invalid input”.

Order placed: the ways back (See this order, all your orders, go back to the portal) also sit in a sentence of plain links. Safari's Reader view hides the buttons and the portal menu, which left buyers with no way out.

entries.title: Print-on-demand orders always ship their printed pieces
items: A piece printed for an order always ships from the packing area, even if its pick record was lost. Before, an order whose cards were all printed could refuse to ship with “Reserved stock is missing from the shelves”.

Pick screen: Fix on a printed piece's stop is refused instead of quietly dropping it. The piece went straight into packing, so there's no shelf to send it back to. For the wrong piece, cancel its print job or change the line.
When stock really is missing at shipping, the message names the SKU, the lot and how many units.

entries.title: Portal fixes: kit names, a way back after ordering, as-is print cards that wait for their artwork
items: Kit and sub-category blocks: long names sit on the left and wrap to two lines instead of being centred and cut off at both ends.
After placing an order: View order, Keep shopping and Back to home. Refreshing the page still says the order was placed, with the same ways back into the portal.
A cart of only e-downloads can be placed — it no longer waits for a ship-to address it doesn't need.

As-is print cards: buyers are no longer asked to “add your details” to a card that has none. When the card's own artwork can't print yet, the buyer is told the warehouse is on it, and the moment the artwork is fixed or accepted with Print anyway, every order waiting for it goes ahead by itself. A waiting print job also has Try again with the SKU's artwork.
Print anyway now carries through to the print-ready copy of the file, so an accepted file actually reaches production.

entries.title: Disconnect a client from the ordering platform
items: Customer → Ordering platform → Connection → Disconnect…: unlink a client from the ordering platform once it's set up — for a brand that has left, or one linked to the wrong company. The card lists what will happen first: the link and the client's own credential go, orders stop coming in, nothing more is sent, and anything still waiting to go out is cancelled. SKUs, stock, orders and people stay.
Which SKU is which ordering platform part is kept so a reconnect picks up without importing again — or tick Also forget to clear it. Connecting again starts at Not live yet, so nothing old is sent.

entries.title: Pace: Staging and Live connected side by side, each customer's Pace ID checked against both; sign-in photos can show the whole image
items: Settings → Integrations → Pace: connect Pace Staging and Pace Live side by side — each with its own address, username and password (stored encrypted) and its own Connect & check. Nothing is written to Pace yet; monthly billing jobs come next and will run against whichever one you pick.

Sign-in page photo fit (Design studio → Sign-in): Fill, as before, or Show whole image — the whole picture with nothing cropped, the page colour around it. For logos and artwork that mustn't be cut off.
Customer → Billing → Pace: the customer's Pace customer ID. Saving checks it in every connected Pace and shows the customer's name there, or says it isn't found, so a typo shows straight away.
